title: Dehydration in children: assess, grade, treat
alt: Flowchart: a child with diarrhoea is assessed for severe dehydration signs (lethargy, sunken eyes, drinking poorly, very slow skin pinch) leading to Plan C with IV Ringer's 100 mL/kg; if two or more "some dehydration" signs, Plan B with ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours; with fewer signs, Plan A at home.
caption: Signs and Plans A–C follow WHO/IMCI diarrhoea management; ORS = oral rehydration salts.

nodes.text: Child with acute diarrhoea or vomiting: assess hydration
Severe dehydration? Two or more: lethargy, sunken eyes, drinks poorly, skin pinch very slow
Plan C: if shocked, 20 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, reassess before repeating
Ringer's 100 mL/kg: 30 mL/kg in 1 h, then 70 mL/kg over 5 h (over 1 year: 30 min, 2.5 h)
Reassess every 15–30 min; start ORS as soon as the child can drink
Admit, monitor closely, treat the cause
Some dehydration? Two or more: restless, sunken eyes, thirsty, skin pinch slow
Plan B: ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 h, small frequent sips by cup and spoon
Reassess at 4 h; keep breastfeeding on demand
Better: Plan A at home. Still some dehydration: repeat Plan B
Plan A at home: extra fluids, ORS after each stool — 50–100 mL under 2 y, 100–200 mL older
Continue feeding; zinc 10–20 mg daily for 10–14 days; return if worse
